<reason>B more convincingly distinguished lower production costs from lower consumer prices while defending stricter enforcement rather than a blanket ban. It answered the scale and prediction questions directly, acknowledging genuine efficiencies and uncertainty. A repeatedly treated integration savings as certain and misrepresented B’s limited concession about subscale firms as surrender. Its appeal to remaining scaled rivals did not establish that they replace the eliminated competitive constraint. B also better balanced acquisition-driven diffusion against lost innovation incentives.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s decisive response was that a merged firm’s ability to charge less does not establish its incentive to do so. After A answered the entry objection by invoking existing scaled rivals, B sharpened the rebuttal: a viable remaining alternative need not replace the pricing pressure exerted by the acquired close competitor.</best_rebuttal>
